subject: Hosted API: request backlog causing p95/p99 regressions — BrightWave escalation
messages:
From: BrightWave Ops <ops@brightwave.io>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 08:12:05 -0700
Subject: Spike in p95/p99 for hosted API — seeing large backlog

Vivek,

We started seeing a sharp jump in p95 and p99 times around 07:45 PDT this morning for calls routed to hosted.region-us-1. The error rate is low (~0.3%) but latency for multi-turn completion requests has doubled at p95 and increased ~3x at p99. Attach are traces and a small packet capture.

Key observations from our side:
- Requests that include long context (>2k tokens) show heavy queuing delays.
- Throughput (requests/sec) is steady — the latency change looks like backlog/queue depth growth.
- We hit a few 502s when requests timed out after 30s.

Can your team confirm whether any batching or autoscaler changes happened in the early morning window? This is impacting a live AB test for us — we need to understand rollback options and ETA for mitigation.

Thanks,
Hannah Lowe
SRE, BrightWave Analytics
attachments: brightwave-traces-0528.log (197KB), p95-p99-heatmap-0528.png (84KB)
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: ops@brightwave.io, Hannah Lowe <hannah.lowe@brightwave.io>
Cc: dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 08:35:41 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in p95/p99 for hosted API — seeing large backlog

Hannah — thank you for the quick heads up and the traces. I pulled the initial telemetry; this looks like a queue depth/batching interaction on the hosted path rather than a model regression.

Immediate next steps from our side:
1) Dylan, can you validate whether the batching config or auto-batcher thresholds changed at ~07:30?
2) Grace, please prepare a short customer-facing note explaining a temporary mitigation (pin to smaller sequence length variant) while we triage.
3) Hannah — we'll provision a canary route that bypasses the large-batch path so we can prove reduced p95; I will follow up with a canary runbook.

I'll loop in Marissa if we need credits/contract relief for the AB test. Vivek
From: dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:01:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in p95/p99 for hosted API — seeing large backlog

Vivek / Grace — quick summary from infra: we did not push a config change to batching thresholds this morning. However, the autoscaler for hosted.region-us-1 applied a more aggressive aggregate-batching policy after a transient increase in inflight short requests at 07:28. The policy groups small requests to improve token efficiency — the grouping algorithm hits worst-case latency when mix of long-context requests increases.

What I'm seeing in the traces: sudden growth in request queue depth on the GPU workers servicing the mixed-tenant pool. The KV cache warmups plus larger sequence requests are causing per-request service time variance; continuous batching is increasing tail latency.

Temporary mitigations we've started:
- Flip routing for BrightWave traffic to a dedicated low-batch lane (canary) that enforces max-batch-size=8 and per-request batching-wait=8ms.
- Abort/timeout tuning: reduce soft batching wait to avoid long queue buildup for high-variance requests.

I'll run the canary now and update with p95/p99 numbers in 20 minutes. Also attaching a quick run of the trace parser.
attachments: canary-run-output.txt (12KB)
From: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: ops@brightwave.io, Hannah Lowe <hannah.lowe@brightwave.io>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:25:07 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in p95/p99 for hosted API — seeing large backlog

Hannah — quick note for your product/AB team: we can route your experimental traffic to a lower-latency path that is less cost-efficient (smaller batches, stronger isolation) until we stabilize. If you choose that route, you may see increased token cost on that traffic.

Do you want us to flip the experiment over now or do you prefer we run the canary and share the before/after metrics? Either way we'll keep you informed.

Grace
Product Ops, Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 12:10:03 -0700
Subject: Escalation: BrightWave p99 regression — request for exec visibility and credits decision

Marissa — BrightWave is on a live AB test; current p95/p99 regressions are customer-visible and they've asked for an ETA and potential credits. I recommend:
- Immediate: approve one-time service credit (equivalent to 2 days of affected usage) as a gesture of goodwill while we confirm root cause.
- Short term: permit dedicated low-batch lane for their experiment (we can toggle via routing policy).
- Follow-up: cross-team postmortem and a permanent mitigation plan for mixed-tenant batching behavior (schedule next week).

Dylan is running the canary and will report numbers. If you approve the credit, I'll draft the communication and pricing change.

Vivek
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>, ops@brightwave.io
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Escalation: BrightWave p99 regression — request for exec visibility and credits decision

Thanks all — appreciate the rapid response. Dylan — thanks for the canary. Hannah, BrightWave team: based on Dylan's canary numbers we are prepared to:
- Issue a one-time credit (2 days of usage) applied to your account within 5 business days.
- Route your AB test to the low-batch lane immediately if you confirm.
- Schedule a technical postmortem with your SRE and our infra team next Wed (invite to follow).

Dylan, please drop the canary output + p95/p99 before/after comparison to the shared drive link and I'll attach the credit approval.

Marissa Cole
